The 'template-rendered' signal allows handlers to perform actions after a template has been rendered in Flask.
The 'before-render-template' signal allows handlers to perform actions before a template is rendered in Flask.
The 'request-started' signal indicates that a request has started processing in Flask.
The 'request-finished' signal indicates that a request has finished processing in Flask.
The 'request-tearing-down' signal indicates that a request is tearing down its context in Flask.
The 'got-request-exception' signal indicates that an exception occurred during the handling of a request in Flask.
The 'appcontext-tearing-down' signal indicates that the application context is being torn down in Flask.
The 'appcontext-pushed' signal indicates that an application context has been pushed in Flask.
The 'appcontext-popped' signal indicates that an application context has been popped in Flask.
The 'message-flashed' signal indicates that a message has been flashed to the user in Flask.
